---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and read messages, reply in threads, manage reactions, list channels and users, and upload files. Use when the user asks to post or send a message to Slack, fetch Slack channel history or messages, notify a Slack channel, list Slack channels or users, react to Slack messages, or upload a file to Slack.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Use Slack's Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`) to post messages, read channel history, manage threads and reactions, list channels and users, and upload files. The bundled script (`scripts/slack_api.js`) handles authentication, channel-name resolution, pagination hints, and friendly error messages so you do not rewrite HTTP plumbing every time.

## Authentication

- Export the token before calling the API: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is used as a fallback by the script).
- Never hardcode tokens in commands, files, or conversation output. Treat them as secrets.
- The token must have the OAuth scopes for the operation (e.g. `chat:write` to post, `channels:history` to read history). See `references/slack-api.md` for the full endpoint-to-scope table.

## Quick Start

Send a message to a channel (name or ID both work):

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.js send-message --channel general --text "Hello from Gemini CLI!"
```

Read the last 10 messages in a channel:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.js channel-history --channel general --limit 10
```

## Common Operations

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Send a message | `send-message --channel <name or id> --text "..."` |
| Send a rich (blocks) message | `send-message --channel <name or id> --blocks '{"blocks":[...]}'` |
| Reply in a thread | `send-message --channel <name or id> --text "..." --thread-ts <ts>` |
| Read channel history | `channel-history --channel <name or id> [--limit N] [--oldest ts] [--latest ts]` |
| Read thread replies | `thread-replies --channel <name or id> --thread-ts <ts> [--limit N]` |
| List channels | `list-channels [--types public_channel,private_channel] [--limit N]` |
| Add a reaction | `add-reaction --channel <name or id> --timestamp <ts> --emoji white_check_mark` |
| Remove a reaction | `remove-reaction --channel <name or id> --timestamp <ts> --emoji white_check_mark` |
| Upload a file | `upload-file --channel <name or id> --file ./report.pdf [--title "Report"]` |
| List users | `list-users [--limit N]` |
| User details | `user-info --user <U...>` |

Append `--json` to any command to print the raw API response instead of a summary.

## Channels, Users, and Timestamps

- `--channel` accepts a channel name (`general` or `#general`) or a channel ID (`C123ABC`). The script resolves names to IDs automatically; prefer IDs in scripts for reliability.
- Message timestamps (`ts`) look like `1710000000.123456`. Use `channel-history` to find a message's ts.
- A thread is identified by its parent message's `ts` — pass it as `--thread-ts`.

## Pagination and Rate Limits

- List and history calls return only the first page. The script prints a hint when more results exist; page with `--cursor` (lists) or `--oldest <ts of last message>` (history) until there is no `next_cursor` / `has_more`.
- Slack rate-limits each method per workspace. On HTTP 429 the script reports the `Retry-After` value — back off and retry, and reduce `--limit` for large reads. Details in `references/slack-api.md`.

## Message Formatting

- Text supports Slack mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<@U123|Name>`, `<#C123>`, `<https://example.com|label>`.
- For rich layouts use `--blocks` with a JSON blocks payload. See `references/slack-api.md` for block-kit essentials and limits.

## Reference

Read `references/slack-api.md` when you need: the full endpoint/scope table, curl equivalents, error-code meanings, rate-limit tiers, or block-kit schemas.

## Script Requirements

`scripts/slack_api.js` requires Node.js 18+ (global `fetch`, `FormData`). It never prints the token, suppresses stack traces, and exits with a single clean `Failure: ...` line on error.

# Slack API Reference

Detailed reference for the Slack Web API. Load this file when you need endpoint details, scopes, error codes, rate-limit behavior, or message formatting rules.

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication and Tokens](#1-authentication-and-tokens)
2. [Endpoints and Scopes](#2-endpoints-and-scopes)
3. [Pagination](#3-pagination)
4. [Rate Limits](#4-rate-limits)
5. [Common Errors](#5-common-errors)
6. [Message Formatting (mrkdwn and Blocks)](#6-message-formatting-mrkdwn-and-blocks)
7. [Threads](#7-threads)
8. [Files](#8-files)
9. [curl Equivalents](#9-curl-equivalents)
10. [IDs and Timestamps](#10-ids-and-timestamps)

## 1. Authentication and Tokens

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`
- Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- POST bodies are `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (except `files.upload`, which is `multipart/form-data`).
- Token types: bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. The app must be installed into the workspace with the required OAuth scopes.
- The script reads `SLACK_TOKEN` (fallback: `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`). Never log tokens.

## 2. Endpoints and Scopes

Use the `conversations.*` family for channels — it works uniformly for public channels, private channels, and DMs (the legacy `channels.*` / `groups.*` APIs are deprecated).

| Endpoint | Purpose | Key scopes (bot) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | Send a message or thread reply | `chat:write` | Requires `channel`; accepts `text` and/or `blocks`; `thread_ts` makes it a thread reply |
| `chat.update` | Edit a message | `chat:write` | Requires `channel` + `ts` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | `chat:write` | Requires `channel` + `ts` |
| `conversations.list` | List channels | `channels:read`, `groups:read` | `types` filter; cursor pagination; `exclude_archived` |
| `conversations.history` | Read channel messages | `channels:history` | `latest`/`oldest` timestamps; `has_more` flag |
| `conversations.replies` | Read a thread | `channels:history` | `ts` = parent message timestamp |
| `conversations.info` | Channel metadata | `channels:read` | |
| `reactions.add` | Add an emoji reaction | `reactions:write` | `timestamp` = message ts |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove an emoji reaction | `reactions:write` | |
| `files.upload` | Upload a file | `files:write` | multipart; `channels` accepts a comma-separated list |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | `users:read` | Cursor pagination |
| `users.info` | User details | `users:read` | |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find user by email | `users:read.email` | |

## 3. Pagination

- List endpoints (`conversations.list`, `users.list`) return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Pass it back as `cursor` until it is empty.
- `conversations.history` returns `has_more: true` when older messages exist; page by passing `latest` = the `ts` of the last message you received.
- Keep `limit` at 200 or below for list calls; history accepts up to 999 per page.
- Loop, don't assume one page is the whole answer.

## 4. Rate Limits

- Slack enforces per-method, per-workspace rate limits organized in tiers (roughly 1 / 20 / 50 / 100+ requests per minute depending on the method; writes like `chat.postMessage` are more restricted than many reads).
- On HTTP 429, the `Retry-After` header gives the wait in seconds. Back off and retry; batch operations and reduce `--limit` for large reads instead of hammering.
- Repeated 429s or `internal_error` responses warrant an exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s).

## 5. Common Errors

| `error` value | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `not_authed` | No or malformed token | Set `SLACK_TOKEN` |
| `invalid_auth` | Token invalid or revoked | Reinstall/re-issue the token |
| `account_inactive` | Token owner account disabled | Check with workspace admin |
| `token_revoked` | Token was revoked | Issue a new token |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope | Grant the scope listed in section 2 |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameter values | Check channel/ts/limit values |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel does not exist or bot cannot see it | Verify ID/name; ensure the bot is in the channel |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived | Unarchive before posting |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not a member | Invite the bot to the channel |
| `user_not_in_channel` | Target user is not in the channel | Use a channel both share |
| `invalid_emoji` | Emoji name unknown in this workspace | Use a valid emoji name |
| `msg_too_long` | Text over 40,000 chars | Shorten or split the message |
| `invalid_blocks` | Blocks payload malformed | Validate the JSON against block-kit schema |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests | Honor `Retry-After` and back off |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace policy blocks the action | Adjust workspace/app settings |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry with backoff |

## 6. Message Formatting (mrkdwn and Blocks)

**mrkdwn** (in `text`): `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~strike~`, `>quote`, bullet lists with `•`, links `<https://example.com|label>`, user mentions `<@U123|Name>`, channel links `<#C123>`.

**Blocks** (in `blocks`): a JSON array under `"blocks"`. Common block types:

- `section` — text plus optional `fields` (up to 10 fields, each ≤ 2,000 chars)
- `divider` — a horizontal rule
- `header` — bold header text (≤ 150 chars)
- `context` — small text/image elements
- `actions` — buttons, select menus, etc.
- `image` — image with `image_url`, `alt_text`

Block text is limited to 3,000 chars per text object. When both `text` and `blocks` are sent, `blocks` is rendered and `text` is used as a fallback/accessibility representation.

## 7. Threads

- A thread is anchored to a parent message's `ts`. To reply, send `chat.postMessage` with `channel` + `text` + `thread_ts` = parent ts.
- Read a thread with `conversations.replies` (`channel` + `ts` = parent ts).
- Bots can reply to any thread in channels they can access; replies are visible in the thread only (use `reply_broadcast=true` once to also post to the channel).

## 8. Files

- `files.upload` is `multipart/form-data`: `file` (the binary), `filename`, `title`, `initial_comment`, and `channels` (comma-separated channel IDs/names).
- File size limits depend on the workspace plan (up to 1 GB per file on paid plans; free workspaces are more limited).
- The response includes `file.id` and `file.permalink` — surface the permalink to the user.

## 9. curl Equivalents

Send a message:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "channel=general" \
  --data-urlencode "text=Hello from curl"
```

List channels:

```bash
curl "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel&limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Read history:

```bash
curl "https://slack.com/api/conversations.history?channel=C123ABC&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Add a reaction:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/reactions.add \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "channel=C123ABC" \
  --data-urlencode "timestamp=1710000000.123456" \
  --data-urlencode "name=white_check_mark"
```

Upload a file:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -F "channels=general" \
  -F "file=@./report.pdf" \
  -F "title=Monthly report"
```

## 10. IDs and Timestamps

- Channel IDs: `C...` (public), `G...` (private/group), `D...` (DM). User IDs: `U...`. Bot IDs: `B...`.
- Timestamps (`ts`) are `seconds.microseconds` strings — treat them as strings, never as numbers (microsecond precision is lost otherwise).
- To resolve a channel name to an ID: `conversations.list` and match `name`. To resolve a user: `users.list` / `users.lookupByEmail`.

name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and read messages, reply in threads, manage reactions, list channels and users, and upload files. Use when the user asks to post or send a message to Slack, fetch Slack channel history or messages, notify a Slack channel, list Slack channels or users, react to Slack messages, or upload a file to Slack.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Use Slack's Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`) to post messages, read channel history, manage threads and reactions, list channels and users, and upload files. The bundled script (`scripts/slack_api.js`) handles authentication, channel-name resolution, pagination hints, and friendly error messages so you do not rewrite HTTP plumbing every time.

## Authentication

- Export the token before calling the API: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is used as a fallback by the script).
- Never hardcode tokens in commands, files, or conversation output. Treat them as secrets.
- The token must have the OAuth scopes for the operation (e.g. `chat:write` to post, `channels:history` to read history). See `references/slack-api.md` for the full endpoint-to-scope table.

## Quick Start

Send a message to a channel (name or ID both work):

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.js send-message --channel general --text "Hello from Gemini CLI!"
```

Read the last 10 messages in a channel:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.js channel-history --channel general --limit 10
```

## Common Operations

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Send a message | `send-message --channel <name or id> --text "..."` |
| Send a rich (blocks) message | `send-message --channel <name or id> --blocks '{"blocks":[...]}'` |
| Reply in a thread | `send-message --channel <name or id> --text "..." --thread-ts <ts>` |
| Read channel history | `channel-history --channel <name or id> [--limit N] [--oldest ts] [--latest ts]` |
| Read thread replies | `thread-replies --channel <name or id> --thread-ts <ts> [--limit N]` |
| List channels | `list-channels [--types public_channel,private_channel] [--limit N]` |
| Add a reaction | `add-reaction --channel <name or id> --timestamp <ts> --emoji white_check_mark` |
| Remove a reaction | `remove-reaction --channel <name or id> --timestamp <ts> --emoji white_check_mark` |
| Upload a file | `upload-file --channel <name or id> --file ./report.pdf [--title "Report"]` |
| List users | `list-users [--limit N]` |
| User details | `user-info --user <U...>` |

Append `--json` to any command to print the raw API response instead of a summary.

## Channels, Users, and Timestamps

- `--channel` accepts a channel name (`general` or `#general`) or a channel ID (`C123ABC`). The script resolves names to IDs automatically; prefer IDs in scripts for reliability.
- Message timestamps (`ts`) look like `1710000000.123456`. Use `channel-history` to find a message's ts.
- A thread is identified by its parent message's `ts` — pass it as `--thread-ts`.

## Pagination and Rate Limits

- List and history calls return only the first page. The script prints a hint when more results exist; page with `--cursor` (lists) or `--oldest <ts of last message>` (history) until there is no `next_cursor` / `has_more`.
- Slack rate-limits each method per workspace. On HTTP 429 the script reports the `Retry-After` value — back off and retry, and reduce `--limit` for large reads. Details in `references/slack-api.md`.

## Message Formatting

- Text supports Slack mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<@U123|Name>`, `<#C123>`, `<https://example.com|label>`.
- For rich layouts use `--blocks` with a JSON blocks payload. See `references/slack-api.md` for block-kit essentials and limits.

## Reference

Read `references/slack-api.md` when you need: the full endpoint/scope table, curl equivalents, error-code meanings, rate-limit tiers, or block-kit schemas.

## Script Requirements

`scripts/slack_api.js` requires Node.js 18+ (global `fetch`, `FormData`). It never prints the token, suppresses stack traces, and exits with a single clean `Failure: ...` line on error.

# Slack API Reference

Detailed reference for the Slack Web API. Load this file when you need endpoint details, scopes, error codes, rate-limit behavior, or message formatting rules.

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication and Tokens](#1-authentication-and-tokens)
2. [Endpoints and Scopes](#2-endpoints-and-scopes)
3. [Pagination](#3-pagination)
4. [Rate Limits](#4-rate-limits)
5. [Common Errors](#5-common-errors)
6. [Message Formatting (mrkdwn and Blocks)](#6-message-formatting-mrkdwn-and-blocks)
7. [Threads](#7-threads)
8. [Files](#8-files)
9. [curl Equivalents](#9-curl-equivalents)
10. [IDs and Timestamps](#10-ids-and-timestamps)

## 1. Authentication and Tokens

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`

- POST bodies are `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (except `files.upload`, which is `multipart/form-data`).
- Token types: bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. The app must be installed into the workspace with the required OAuth scopes.
- The script reads `SLACK_TOKEN` (fallback: `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`). Never log tokens.

## 2. Endpoints and Scopes

Use the `conversations.*` family for channels — it works uniformly for public channels, private channels, and DMs (the legacy `channels.*` / `groups.*` APIs are deprecated).

| Endpoint | Purpose | Key scopes (bot) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | Send a message or thread reply | `chat:write` | Requires `channel`; accepts `text` and/or `blocks`; `thread_ts` makes it a thread reply |
| `chat.update` | Edit a message | `chat:write` | Requires `channel` + `ts` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | `chat:write` | Requires `channel` + `ts` |
| `conversations.list` | List channels | `channels:read`, `groups:read` | `types` filter; cursor pagination; `exclude_archived` |
| `conversations.history` | Read channel messages | `channels:history` | `latest`/`oldest` timestamps; `has_more` flag |
| `conversations.replies` | Read a thread | `channels:history` | `ts` = parent message timestamp |
| `conversations.info` | Channel metadata | `channels:read` | |
| `reactions.add` | Add an emoji reaction | `reactions:write` | `timestamp` = message ts |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove an emoji reaction | `reactions:write` | |
| `files.upload` | Upload a file | `files:write` | multipart; `channels` accepts a comma-separated list |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | `users:read` | Cursor pagination |
| `users.info` | User details | `users:read` | |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find user by email | `users:read.email` | |

## 3. Pagination

- List endpoints (`conversations.list`, `users.list`) return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Pass it back as `cursor` until it is empty.
- `conversations.history` returns `has_more: true` when older messages exist; page by passing `latest` = the `ts` of the last message you received.
- Keep `limit` at 200 or below for list calls; history accepts up to 999 per page.
- Loop, don't assume one page is the whole answer.

## 4. Rate Limits

- Slack enforces per-method, per-workspace rate limits organized in tiers (roughly 1 / 20 / 50 / 100+ requests per minute depending on the method; writes like `chat.postMessage` are more restricted than many reads).
- On HTTP 429, the `Retry-After` header gives the wait in seconds. Back off and retry; batch operations and reduce `--limit` for large reads instead of hammering.
- Repeated 429s or `internal_error` responses warrant an exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s).

## 5. Common Errors

| `error` value | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `not_authed` | No or malformed token | Set `SLACK_TOKEN` |
| `invalid_auth` | Token invalid or revoked | Reinstall/re-issue the token |
| `account_inactive` | Token owner account disabled | Check with workspace admin |
| `token_revoked` | Token was revoked | Issue a new token |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope | Grant the scope listed in section 2 |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameter values | Check channel/ts/limit values |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel does not exist or bot cannot see it | Verify ID/name; ensure the bot is in the channel |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived | Unarchive before posting |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not a member | Invite the bot to the channel |
| `user_not_in_channel` | Target user is not in the channel | Use a channel both share |
| `invalid_emoji` | Emoji name unknown in this workspace | Use a valid emoji name |
| `msg_too_long` | Text over 40,000 chars | Shorten or split the message |
| `invalid_blocks` | Blocks payload malformed | Validate the JSON against block-kit schema |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests | Honor `Retry-After` and back off |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace policy blocks the action | Adjust workspace/app settings |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry with backoff |

## 6. Message Formatting (mrkdwn and Blocks)

**mrkdwn** (in `text`): `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~strike~`, `>quote`, bullet lists with `•`, links `<https://example.com|label>`, user mentions `<@U123|Name>`, channel links `<#C123>`.

**Blocks** (in `blocks`): a JSON array under `"blocks"`. Common block types:

- `section` — text plus optional `fields` (up to 10 fields, each ≤ 2,000 chars)
- `divider` — a horizontal rule
- `header` — bold header text (≤ 150 chars)
- `context` — small text/image elements
- `actions` — buttons, select menus, etc.
- `image` — image with `image_url`, `alt_text`

Block text is limited to 3,000 chars per text object. When both `text` and `blocks` are sent, `blocks` is rendered and `text` is used as a fallback/accessibility representation.

## 7. Threads

- A thread is anchored to a parent message's `ts`. To reply, send `chat.postMessage` with `channel` + `text` + `thread_ts` = parent ts.
- Read a thread with `conversations.replies` (`channel` + `ts` = parent ts).
- Bots can reply to any thread in channels they can access; replies are visible in the thread only (use `reply_broadcast=true` once to also post to the channel).

## 8. Files

- `files.upload` is `multipart/form-data`: `file` (the binary), `filename`, `title`, `initial_comment`, and `channels` (comma-separated channel IDs/names).
- File size limits depend on the workspace plan (up to 1 GB per file on paid plans; free workspaces are more limited).
- The response includes `file.id` and `file.permalink` — surface the permalink to the user.

## 9. curl Equivalents

Send a message:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "channel=general" \
  --data-urlencode "text=Hello from curl"
```

List channels:

```bash
curl "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel&limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Read history:

```bash
curl "https://slack.com/api/conversations.history?channel=C123ABC&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Add a reaction:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/reactions.add \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "channel=C123ABC" \
  --data-urlencode "timestamp=1710000000.123456" \
  --data-urlencode "name=white_check_mark"
```

Upload a file:

```bash
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -F "channels=general" \
  -F "file=@./report.pdf" \
  -F "title=Monthly report"
```

## 10. IDs and Timestamps

- Channel IDs: `C...` (public), `G...` (private/group), `D...` (DM). User IDs: `U...`. Bot IDs: `B...`.
- Timestamps (`ts`) are `seconds.microseconds` strings — treat them as strings, never as numbers (microsecond precision is lost otherwise).
- To resolve a channel name to an ID: `conversations.list` and match `name`. To resolve a user: `users.list` / `users.lookupByEmail`.
